title: Request Cyclopedia — Customer Synthesis Notebook (Dec 2026)
summary: Compact synthesis of vignettes + a pragmatic feature request matrix focused on short-cycle fixes for runtime/latency customer asks. Emphasis on low-effort patches and measurable SLO impact.
content:
Purpose: quick, action-oriented notebook to translate raw customer threads into implementable patches and hypothesis-led experiments. This is not an exhaustive roadmap — meant for CS/solutions + one-sprint engineering probes.

Method: reviewed 48 support threads (last 90 days) flagged as latency/cost regressions, 12 customer interviews (postmortem style), and 6 internal SRE incident summaries. Distilled common motifs, concrete reproduce steps where available, and mapped to ownerable work items.

Observed motifs (short notes):
- KV/prefix cache confusion: customers expect cache to persist across rapid model-rolls; many naive SDK re-inits flush the cache.
- Burst tail latency with small-batch traffic: autoscaling + batching heuristics misalign for interactive low-rps apps.
- Token-usage surprises: embeddings vs text-gen billing ambiguity in some SDK patterns.
- Fallback churn: clients configured fallbacks to cheaper model variants cause token and context resets, worsening quality unexpectedly.

Representative vignettes (condensed):
1) Fintech customer A: occasional 2–3s tail spikes during streaming responses after model rollouts. Repro: occurs when 2nd request arrives <250ms after first; root cause suspected: runtime cache warming + kernel selection thrash.
2) Marketplace startup B: high unit costs for long multi-turn conversations; they lard prompts with repeated system context because they lack a simple prefix caching API.
3) Healthcare customer C: asked for deterministic downgrade path when private deployment loses Dedicated capacity; current fallback causes user-visible hallucinations.

Distilled asks (ranked by frequency + customer impact):
- Persistent prefix cache (user-controlled pinning) — (freq: high, impact: high)
- Burst-aware autoscaling knobs / latency-first routing policy — (freq: medium, impact: high)
- Billing clarification for embeddings vs generation when using mixed endpoints — (freq: medium, impact: medium)
- Canary-based KV cache warming hook for rollouts — (freq: low, impact: medium)
- Fine-grained fallback fidelity controls (quality thresholds) — (freq: low, impact: high for regulated customers)

Feature request matrix (pragmatic tiles):
- Persistent Prefix Cache (PP-01): short description: API to mark prompt prefixes as long-lived and cached across calls and model-rolls (user pin). Proposed quickship: SDK-level flag + runtime validation; scope v0: keys per-namespace, TTL override. Estimated complexity: 2 eng-weeks. Impact: reduces token resends and cost for multi-turn apps. Suggested owner: eng-serving-runtime / solutions-eng. Linked artifact: JIRA-CS-9821.

- Burst Latency Knob (BL-02): short description: allow per-route latency SLO bucket to prefer latency vs throughput in batching. Quickpatch: add route flag that disables large-group batching under threshold. Complexity: 1 eng-week + one SRE config change. Impact: reduces tail latency for low-rps interactive routes. Suggested owner: platform-engineering.

- Embedding Billing FAQ + SDK safeguard (EB-03): short description: docs + small SDK guard that warns when send_embeddings=true combined with text generation endpoints. Quickpatch: doc page + SDK lint + telemetry event. Complexity: 3 engineer days. Impact: lowers billing confusion and reduces sweet-spot support volume.

- Rollout Cache Warm Hook (RC-04): short description: expose a rollout hook that replays cached prefixes to new model variant to avoid cold-tail spikes. Quickpatch: add lifecycle hook and a small replay worker (non-blocking). Complexity: 2-3 eng-weeks. Impact: reduces post-rollout tail spikes.

- Fallback Fidelity Thresholds (FF-05): short description: route-level policy that defines minimum quality signals for fallback; if fallback would be below threshold, return configurable error / queue instead. Complexity: 3-4 eng-weeks + eval pipeline changes. Impact: high for regulated customers; reduces hallucination risk on fallback.

Quick wins (week-to-week experiments):
- Doc update + SDK warning for embeddings misusage (EB-03) — do first (low effort).
- Add per-route batching override toggle (BL-02 minimal) behind feature flag; run with 5 customers.
- Pre-rollout perf checklist for release engineering: add a KB step to pre-warm common prefixes (manual for now).

Risk notes:
- Persistent cache exposes potential data residency concerns (must tie to customer namespace and encryption). Check KMS/HSM impact if caching persists across private deployments.
- Fast toggles for batching may increase cost; need cost telemetry to be part of rollout.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- What telemetry events would best detect cache-flush regressions automatically? (Ping SRE/observability).
- Can we simulate rollout replay in staging using sampled customer prefixes without leaking PII? (Data-privacy team input needed).

Action items (owners & near-term):
- Ava M. (CS) to open customer-facing FAQ page and coordinate sample reproducer snippets — due: 2026-12-07.
- Liam C. (Solutions Eng) to prototype per-route batching toggle and test with two low-rps customers — due: 2026-12-14.
- Priya G. (Product-Optimize) to scope rollout-warm hook and privacy constraints; write initial PRD (1 page) — due: 2026-12-10.
- Marco R. (SRE) to draft telemetry spec for cache-warmth metrics and tail-latency correlation — due: 2026-12-09.

Customer comms sketch (for CS):
- Short email template: acknowledge spike, request SDK/sequence pattern, propose: "We can toggle per-route batching for your account to see immediate tail improvement; would you like us to enable a trial for two days?"

Appendix: quick reproducer snippets (kept short):
- Reproducer for cold-tail after rollout: 1) send streaming gen with prefix X, 2) immediately trigger model variant switch, 3) send second request within 250ms — observe increased 95p latency. Footnote: share with eng if you need sample logs.

Notes-to-self / collaboration cues:
- Keep this doc lean; convert to Confluence if Priya asks for PRD expansion.
- Capture early experiment metrics in the release desk (observability) and link results to this doc.

End of notebook.
